thread:
UCLA is 5th.

We counted every place to eat within a 10-minute walk (half a mile) of all nine UC campuses:

1. UC Berkeley: 277
2. UC Davis: 43
3. UC Irvine: 37
4. UC San Diego: 29
5. UCLA: 14
6. UC Riverside: 12
7. UC Santa Barbara: 2
8. UC Santa Cruz: 1
9. UC Merced: 0

Measured from each campus's center, using Overture Maps listings.

Look up any campus, with the closest places first: https://www.savorscout.net/campus/ca

Florida State has more restaurants within a 10-minute walk of campus than UF. By two.

Every Florida university with 20,000+ students:

1. Florida State: 50
2. Florida: 48
3. FIU: 45
4. UCF: 30
5. USF: 16
6. Florida Atlantic: 7
6. Nova Southeastern: 7

Measured from each campus's center, using Overture Maps listings.

Look up any campus, with the closest places first: https://www.savorscout.net/campus/fl

Penn State beats Penn, Pitt and Drexel for restaurants within a 10-minute walk of campus.

Every Pennsylvania university with 20,000+ students:

1. Penn State: 156
2. Pitt: 135
2. Drexel: 135
4. Penn: 125
5. Temple: 91

Measured from each campus's center, using Overture Maps listings.

Look up any campus, with the closest places first: https://www.savorscout.net/campus/pa
How to tell good pho before you order. It's all in the broth:
It should be clear and still taste of beef. Cloudy broth was boiled too hard, and boiled broth tastes muddy no matter how long it cooked.
You should smell the spices before you taste them: star anise, cinnamon, clove. Broth that smells only of salt came from a stock cube.
Herbs come on the side, so you add basil, bean sprouts and lime fresh. And the noodles shouldn't be clumped: that means they were cooked ahead.

First time at a new place? Order pho tai, thin rare beef that cooks in the broth. It shows how hot the broth really is.

More on finding good pho: https://www.savorscout.net/food/pho
